/-!
# Universal point set

In graph drawing, a *universal point set of order $n$* (or *$n$-universal point set*) is a set
$S$ of points in the Euclidean plane such that every $n$-vertex planar graph has a crossing-free
straight-line drawing with all vertices placed at (distinct) points of $S$.

Grids of size $O(n) \times O(n)$ are $n$-universal, so $n$-universal point sets of size $O(n^2)$
exist; the smallest known ones have size $n^2/4 - \Theta(n)$ [BCDE14]. The best known lower bound
is $1.293n - o(n)$ [SSS20]. Rectangular grids of subquadratic size are never universal, but this
does not rule out subquadratic universal point sets of other types. The problem from Wikipedia's
list of unsolved problems asks whether $n$-universal point sets of *subquadratic* size, that is of
size $o(n^2)$, exist.

Mathlib has no notion of planarity. Planarity is defined here through crossing-free drawings in
the plane with edges drawn as simple arcs. By Fáry's theorem (recorded below as a solved
statement) this is the same as having a crossing-free straight-line drawing.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Universal point set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_point_set)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [BCDE14] M. J. Bannister, Z. Cheng, W. E. Devanny, D. Eppstein, *Superpatterns and universal
  point sets*, J. Graph Algorithms Appl. 18 (2014), 177–209.
  [arXiv:1308.0403](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0403)
- [SSS20] M. Scheucher, H. Schrezenmaier, R. Steiner, *A note on universal point sets for planar
  graphs*, J. Graph Algorithms Appl. 24 (2020), 247–267.
  [arXiv:1811.06482](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.06482)
-/

structure IsPlaneDrawing (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) (A : Sym2 V → Set ℝ²) :
    Prop where
  injective : Function.Injective f
  isArc : ∀ u v, G.Adj u v →
    ∃ γ : Path (f u) (f v), Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = A s(u, v)
  mem_of_mem_arc : ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ∀ w, f w ∈ A e → w ∈ e
  inter_subset : ∀ e₁ ∈ G.edgeSet, ∀ e₂ ∈ G.edgeSet, e₁ ≠ e₂ →
    A e₁ ∩ A e₂ ⊆ f '' {w | w ∈ e₁ ∧ w ∈ e₂}

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `Path`, `SimpleGraph.edgeSet`, `Sym2` (used as building blocks); no planar embedding notion exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (grepped for 'planar', 'IsPlanar', 'embedding.*plane').

blocks.name: IsPlaneDrawing
blocks.text:
/--
A crossing-free drawing of the simple graph `G` in the plane. The map `f` places the vertices at
distinct points, and `A e` is the curve drawn for the edge `e`:
* the curve of the edge `{u, v}` is a simple arc (the image of an injective path) from `f u` to
  `f v`;
* the curve of an edge contains no vertex other than its two endpoints;
* the curves of two distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints.
-/
structure IsPlaneDrawing (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) (A : Sym2 V → Set ℝ²) :
    Prop where
  injective : Function.Injective f
  isArc : ∀ u v, G.Adj u v →
    ∃ γ : Path (f u) (f v), Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = A s(u, v)
  mem_of_mem_arc : ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ∀ w, f w ∈ A e → w ∈ e
  inter_subset : ∀ e₁ ∈ G.edgeSet, ∀ e₂ ∈ G.edgeSet, e₁ ≠ e₂ →
    A e₁ ∩ A e₂ ⊆ f '' {w | w ∈ e₁ ∧ w ∈ e₂}

def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ f A, IsPlaneDrawing G f A
blocks.docstring: A simple graph is *planar* if it has a crossing-free drawing in the plane.

def IsStraightLineDrawing (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → f w ∈ segment ℝ (f u) (f v) → w = u ∨ w = v) ∧
    ∀ u v x y, G.Adj u v → G.Adj x y → s(u, v) ≠ s(x, y) →
      segment ℝ (f u) (f v) ∩ segment ℝ (f x) (f y) ⊆ f '' ({u, v} ∩ {x, y})

blocks.docstring:
A finite set `S` of points in the plane is *`n`-universal* if every planar graph on `n` vertices
has a crossing-free straight-line drawing with all vertices placed at (distinct) points of `S`.

justification.name: UniversalPointSet.IsUniversal
justification.why_needed: Defines an n-universal point set (a finite set of points admitting crossing-free straight-line drawings of every n-vertex planar graph), the central object of the conjecture.

blocks.name: IsUniversal
blocks.text:
/--
A finite set `S` of points in the plane is *`n`-universal* if every planar graph on `n` vertices
has a crossing-free straight-line drawing with all vertices placed at (distinct) points of `S`.
-/
def IsUniversal (n : ℕ) (S : Finset ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), IsPlanar G →
    ∃ f : Fin n → ℝ², IsStraightLineDrawing G f ∧ ∀ v, f v ∈ S

theorem universal_point_set :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : ℕ → Finset ℝ², (∀ n, IsUniversal n (S n)) ∧
      (fun n => ((S n).card : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ 2) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Universal point sets of subquadratic size for planar graphs.**

Do there exist $n$-universal point sets $S_n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, one for each $n$, whose
sizes are subquadratic, i.e. $|S_n| = o(n^2)$? The point set $S_n$ may depend on $n$ and need not
be a grid. Equivalently, is the minimum size $f(n)$ of an $n$-universal point set $o(n^2)$?

The known bounds are linear from below ($f(n) \ge 1.293n - o(n)$, [SSS20]) and quadratic from
above ($f(n) \le n^2/4 - \Theta(n)$, [BCDE14]).

@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem IsStraightLineDrawing.isPlanar {G : SimpleGraph V} {f : V → ℝ²}
    (h : IsStraightLineDrawing G f) : IsPlanar G := by
  obtain ⟨hinj, hvert, hcross⟩ := h
  refine ⟨f, Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v => segment ℝ (f u) (f v), fun u v => segment_symm ℝ _ _⟩,
    hinj, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro u v huv
    refine ⟨Path.segment (f u) (f v), ?_, by simp⟩
    exact (AffineMap.lineMap_injective ℝ (hinj.ne huv.ne)).comp Subtype.val_injective
  · intro e he w hw
    induction e using Sym2.ind with
    | _ u v =>
      simp only [Sym2.lift_mk] at hw
      simpa using hvert u v w he hw
  · intro e₁ he₁ e₂ he₂ hne p hp
    induction e₁ using Sym2.ind with
    | _ u v =>
      induction e₂ using Sym2.ind with
      | _ x y =>
        simp only [Sym2.lift_mk] at hp
        obtain ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩ := hcross u v x y he₁ he₂ hne hp
        exact ⟨w, by simpa using hw, rfl⟩

@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem isPlanar_bot (n : ℕ) : IsPlanar (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) := by
  refine IsStraightLineDrawing.isPlanar (f := fun i => EuclideanSpace.single (0 : Fin 2) (i : ℝ))
    ⟨?_, fun _ _ _ h => h.elim, fun _ _ _ _ h => h.elim⟩
  intro i j h
  have := congrArg (fun p : ℝ² => p 0) h
  exact Fin.ext (by simpa using this)
blocks.docstring: The graph with no edges is planar.

@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem le_card_of_isUniversal {n : ℕ} {S : Finset ℝ²} (hS : IsUniversal n S) :
    n ≤ S.card := by
  obtain ⟨f, ⟨hinj, -, -⟩, hfS⟩ := hS ⊥ (isPlanar_bot n)
  simpa using Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (s := Finset.univ) f (fun v _ => hfS v) hinj.injOn
blocks.docstring: An `n`-universal point set has at least `n` points.
blocks.name: le_card_of_isUniversal
blocks.text:

@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem le_card_of_isUniversal {n : ℕ} {S : Finset ℝ²} (hS : IsUniversal n S) :
    n ≤ S.card := by
  obtain ⟨f, ⟨hinj, -, -⟩, hfS⟩ := hS ⊥ (isPlanar_bot n)
  simpa using Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (s := Finset.univ) f (fun v _ => hfS v) hinj.injOn

@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem IsUniversal.mono {n : ℕ} {S T : Finset ℝ²} (hS : IsUniversal n S) (hST : S ⊆ T) :
    IsUniversal n T := by
  intro G hG
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfS⟩ := hS G hG
  exact ⟨f, hf, fun v => hST (hfS v)⟩
blocks.docstring: Every superset of an `n`-universal point set is `n`-universal.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question: does there exist, for every n, an n-universal point set (finite S ⊂ ℝ² such that every n-vertex planar graph has a crossing-free straight-line drawing with vertices at distinct points of S) whose cardinality is o(n²), i.e. is the minimum size f(n) subquadratic; 'subquadratic' should be read as little-o of n² (not merely below the known n²/4 − Θ(n) bound), the point set may depend on n and need not be a grid (grids are known to require Ω(n²)), and the open status means the answer should be left as answer(sorry) rather than asserted; the article's broader 'close the gap between linear lower and quadratic upper bounds' / 'determine f(n)' is the same problem and is not a separate question posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful shape: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : ℕ → Finset ℝ², (∀ n, S n is n-universal) ∧ (card (S n) : ℝ) =o[atTop] n². This matches the decomposition notes (set may depend on n, arbitrary finite planar point set, little-o of n², open answer). c05 was chosen as base because it defines planarity topologically (vertices at distinct points, edges as injective Paths, arcs meet only at images of common endpoints, no vertex in a non-incident arc), so 'n-vertex planar graph' is matched definitionally rather than through Fáry's theorem; Fáry's theorem is recorded as a research-solved statement connecting it to the crossing-free straight-line drawing predicate used for the universality condition. c05 also has fully proved API/test lemmas (straight-line drawing ⇒ planar, edgeless graph planar, n-universal ⇒ ≥ n points, monotonicity, ∅ is 0-universal) that validate non-vacuity. Other candidates (c01,c02,c04,c06,c08) are equally correct with a Fáry-based definition of planarity; c03 is correct with open segments and Set.ncard; c07 omits the vertex-on-non-incident-edge clause (extensionally harmless but less standard); c04 uses ℝ × ℝ rather than the repo's ℝ² notation. Sorry'd literature variants from c06/c08 were not shipped since they are not slots and add faithfulness risk.

open Filter Asymptotics
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace UniversalPointSet

variable {V : Type*}

/--
A crossing-free drawing of the simple graph `G` in the plane. The map `f` places the vertices at
distinct points, and `A e` is the curve drawn for the edge `e`:
* the curve of the edge `{u, v}` is a simple arc (the image of an injective path) from `f u` to
  `f v`;
* the curve of an edge contains no vertex other than its two endpoints;
* the curves of two distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints.
-/
structure IsPlaneDrawing (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) (A : Sym2 V → Set ℝ²) :
    Prop where
  injective : Function.Injective f
  isArc : ∀ u v, G.Adj u v →
    ∃ γ : Path (f u) (f v), Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = A s(u, v)
  mem_of_mem_arc : ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ∀ w, f w ∈ A e → w ∈ e
  inter_subset : ∀ e₁ ∈ G.edgeSet, ∀ e₂ ∈ G.edgeSet, e₁ ≠ e₂ →
    A e₁ ∩ A e₂ ⊆ f '' {w | w ∈ e₁ ∧ w ∈ e₂}

/-- A simple graph is *planar* if it has a crossing-free drawing in the plane. -/
def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ f A, IsPlaneDrawing G f A

/--
`f` is a crossing-free straight-line drawing of the simple graph `G` in the plane: the vertices are
placed at distinct points, every edge `{u, v}` is drawn as the closed line segment from `f u` to
`f v`, no such segment contains a vertex other than its two endpoints, and the segments of two
distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints.
-/
def IsStraightLineDrawing (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → f w ∈ segment ℝ (f u) (f v) → w = u ∨ w = v) ∧
    ∀ u v x y, G.Adj u v → G.Adj x y → s(u, v) ≠ s(x, y) →
      segment ℝ (f u) (f v) ∩ segment ℝ (f x) (f y) ⊆ f '' ({u, v} ∩ {x, y})

/--
A finite set `S` of points in the plane is *`n`-universal* if every planar graph on `n` vertices
has a crossing-free straight-line drawing with all vertices placed at (distinct) points of `S`.
-/
def IsUniversal (n : ℕ) (S : Finset ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), IsPlanar G →
    ∃ f : Fin n → ℝ², IsStraightLineDrawing G f ∧ ∀ v, f v ∈ S

/--
**Universal point sets of subquadratic size for planar graphs.**

Do there exist $n$-universal point sets $S_n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, one for each $n$, whose
sizes are subquadratic, i.e. $|S_n| = o(n^2)$? The point set $S_n$ may depend on $n$ and need not
be a grid. Equivalently, is the minimum size $f(n)$ of an $n$-universal point set $o(n^2)$?

The known bounds are linear from below ($f(n) \ge 1.293n - o(n)$, [SSS20]) and quadratic from
above ($f(n) \le n^2/4 - \Theta(n)$, [BCDE14]).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52 68]
theorem universal_point_set :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : ℕ → Finset ℝ², (∀ n, IsUniversal n (S n)) ∧
      (fun n => ((S n).card : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ 2) := by
  sorry

/--
**Fáry's theorem.** A finite simple graph is planar if and only if it has a crossing-free
straight-line drawing in the plane.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem isPlanar_iff_exists_isStraightLineDrawing [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsPlanar G ↔ ∃ f : V → ℝ², IsStraightLineDrawing G f := by
  sorry

/-- A crossing-free straight-line drawing is a crossing-free drawing. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem IsStraightLineDrawing.isPlanar {G : SimpleGraph V} {f : V → ℝ²}
    (h : IsStraightLineDrawing G f) : IsPlanar G := by
  obtain ⟨hinj, hvert, hcross⟩ := h
  refine ⟨f, Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v => segment ℝ (f u) (f v), fun u v => segment_symm ℝ _ _⟩,
    hinj, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro u v huv
    refine ⟨Path.segment (f u) (f v), ?_, by simp⟩
    exact (AffineMap.lineMap_injective ℝ (hinj.ne huv.ne)).comp Subtype.val_injective
  · intro e he w hw
    induction e using Sym2.ind with
    | _ u v =>
      simp only [Sym2.lift_mk] at hw
      simpa using hvert u v w he hw
  · intro e₁ he₁ e₂ he₂ hne p hp
    induction e₁ using Sym2.ind with
    | _ u v =>
      induction e₂ using Sym2.ind with
      | _ x y =>
        simp only [Sym2.lift_mk] at hp
        obtain ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩ := hcross u v x y he₁ he₂ hne hp
        exact ⟨w, by simpa using hw, rfl⟩

/-- The graph with no edges is planar. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem isPlanar_bot (n : ℕ) : IsPlanar (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) := by
  refine IsStraightLineDrawing.isPlanar (f := fun i => EuclideanSpace.single (0 : Fin 2) (i : ℝ))
    ⟨?_, fun _ _ _ h => h.elim, fun _ _ _ _ h => h.elim⟩
  intro i j h
  have := congrArg (fun p : ℝ² => p 0) h
  exact Fin.ext (by simpa using this)

/-- An `n`-universal point set has at least `n` points. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem le_card_of_isUniversal {n : ℕ} {S : Finset ℝ²} (hS : IsUniversal n S) :
    n ≤ S.card := by
  obtain ⟨f, ⟨hinj, -, -⟩, hfS⟩ := hS ⊥ (isPlanar_bot n)
  simpa using Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (s := Finset.univ) f (fun v _ => hfS v) hinj.injOn

/-- Every superset of an `n`-universal point set is `n`-universal. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem IsUniversal.mono {n : ℕ} {S T : Finset ℝ²} (hS : IsUniversal n S) (hST : S ⊆ T) :
    IsUniversal n T := by
  intro G hG
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfS⟩ := hS G hG
  exact ⟨f, hf, fun v => hST (hfS v)⟩

/-- The empty set is `0`-universal. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem isUniversal_zero_empty : IsUniversal 0 ∅ := by
  intro G _
  exact ⟨Fin.elim0, ⟨fun a => a.elim0, fun u => u.elim0, fun u => u.elim0⟩,
    fun v => v.elim0⟩

end UniversalPointSet

items: 'Subquadratic' is read as little-o of n² (`=o[atTop]` on ℕ), per the decomposition table, not as O(n^{2-ε}) and not merely 'below n²/4'.

'Existence of subquadratic universal point sets' is formalized as the existence of a sequence S : ℕ → Finset ℝ² with S n being n-universal and |S n| = o(n²), rather than via a minimum-size function f(n) = sInf{...} = o(n²). The two are equivalent (given S n, f n ≤ |S n|; conversely pick minimal sets), and the chosen form avoids sInf junk values.
Point sets are `Finset ℝ²` (ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), the repo's scoped notation); finiteness is implicit in asking about the size.
n-vertex planar graphs are modeled as `SimpleGraph (Fin n)`; every n-vertex graph is isomorphic to one on Fin n and drawings transfer along isomorphisms.

Planarity is defined topologically (`IsPlanar G := ∃ f A, IsPlaneDrawing G f A`): vertices at distinct points, each edge drawn as a simple arc (range of an injective `Path (f u) (f v)`), no arc passes through a vertex other than its endpoints, and two distinct arcs meet only in the images of common endpoints. This is the standard definition of a plane graph (e.g. Diestel). Fáry's theorem (equivalence with straight-line drawability for finite graphs) is recorded as a separate `research solved` statement, not used as the definition.

A crossing-free straight-line drawing (`IsStraightLineDrawing`) requires: f injective; for every edge uv and vertex w, f w ∈ segment(f u, f v) → w ∈ {u,v}; for distinct edges uv ≠ xy (as Sym2), segment ∩ segment ⊆ f '' ({u,v} ∩ {x,y}). The vertex-not-on-edge condition is slightly stronger than the literature phrasing 'no two edges intersect except at a common endpoint' only for isolated vertices; it does not change which point sets are n-universal (embed the graph in a connected planar supergraph and restrict), and it is the standard plane-graph condition.
Vertices are required to be placed at distinct points of S (injectivity), matching 'vertices at distinct points of S'.
Category `research open` with `answer(sorry)` since the problem is open; AMS tags 5 (combinatorics/graph theory), 52 (discrete geometry), 68 (computer science/graph drawing).

Extra declarations: Fáry's theorem (`research solved`, sorry), API lemmas `IsStraightLineDrawing.isPlanar` (proved), `isPlanar_bot` (proved), `le_card_of_isUniversal` (proved: an n-universal set has ≥ n points), `IsUniversal.mono` (proved), and a test `isUniversal_zero_empty` (proved).

Modeling choices a human should confirm: (1) planarity is a bespoke topological definition (no Mathlib notion exists); the straight-line-drawing predicate used in IsUniversal requires additionally that no vertex lies on a non-incident edge segment, which is the standard plane-drawing convention and does not change which point sets are universal; (2) n-vertex graphs are SimpleGraph (Fin n); (3) the o(n²) condition is stated as existence of a sequence of n-universal Finsets rather than via an sInf-based minimum-size function, avoiding junk values (equivalent since minimizers exist). Fáry's theorem is included as a research-solved statement with [Finite V]; its backward direction is proved in-file.
